source.section: PIT-1 instructions PDF page 25, line 14; PDF page 26, Low- and Middle-Income Tax Exemption Worksheet lines 1 to 8; PDF page 22, line 5; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - standard deduction 23,625.00 = 16,375.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, head of household. Line 9 federal AGI 40,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 23,625.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 low- and middle-income worksheet: line 1 40,000.00; line 2 30,000.00; line 3 10,000.00; line 4 0.10; line 5 1,000.00; line 6 2,500.00 - 1,000.00 = 1,500.00; line 7 1 exemption(s); line 8 = 1,500.00. Line 15 PIT-ADJ deductions and exemptions 0.00. Line 17 = 40,000.00 + 0.00 - 23,625.00 - 1,500.00 - 0.00 = 14,875.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 16,375.00 = 16,375.00; less base deductions 1,500.00 gives 14,875.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 6,875.00 = 220; total 340, to the cent 340.00. The table row over 14,800 to 14,900 gives 339; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 340.00. One exemption, because checks carry no dependents; the dependents' share is not_modelled.
